source_refs.locator: BTR printed p. 116, Table 31, agriculture summary.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-01-16 reports: Maize covers ~45% of arable land, mainly in water-short areas; family farms manage nearly 90% of it and generally have low adaptive capacity. Driest-year yields fell up to 40% against 2011–2020.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: BTR printed p. 117, Table 31, fruit-production risk summary.

geographies: areas south of the Sava and Danube rivers
evidence.scenario: Mid-century; no scenario specified in the BTR summary.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-01-16 reports: South of Sava and Danube, apricot and almond face the highest growing-season frost risk; listed fruits cover ~10% of fruit area. Risk is expected high across most Serbia by mid-century.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-01-16 reports: For 2024–2026, RSD 998m was allocated (89.3% national, 10.7% donor); BTR calls funding insufficient and says major monitoring-capacity investment was absent.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 22 and 124 (printed p. 125), summary and Appendix P1.3.2/Figure P1.10.

evidence.scenario: The map compares 2001–2020 with 2041–2060 under RCP8.5.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: The programme reports high/very-high extreme-precipitation risk on 7% of Serbia in 2001–2020, including central/western Serbia, parts of Vojvodina and eastern Serbia; it projects 56% in 2041–2060 under RCP8.5, citing Životić and Vuković-Vimić (2022).
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 22, programme summary table, drought entry.

evidence.scenario: RCP8.5 for 2081–2100; no scenario specified for nearer periods.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: One strong-drought year occurred in 2011–2020; the programme projects 2–3 per decade in 2021–2040, 3–4 in 2041–2060, and 7–8 per decade under RCP8.5 in 2081–2100.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 134, Appendix A1.6, recommendations on hazards requiring local risk assessment.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2023 reports: Flood, landslide and erosion risks depend on local terrain and protection works; the programme recommends assessment at local-government level.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

pathways.compact_statement: Flood evacuation into isolated, poorly lit or unsupported centres can heighten women's protection risks; the 2014 study does not measure violence incidence.
alternative_explanations: Centre design, support quality and pre-existing exclusion independently affect risk.
Historical study is not nationally representative or a current shelter assessment.
pathways.uncertainty: Conditional protection mechanism from a dated event-specific study, not verified violence occurrence or anthropogenic climate attribution.
recommendations: No structural linkage issue identified; review each cited passage for its specific causal link, alternatives and uncertainty before treating the pathway as verified.
